reasons: The rule targets an absent exit/data-return clause; the cited § 3.5 (Effect of Termination) addresses only accrued payment obligations and contains no transition assistance, data return/export, or deletion mechanic, so a 'missing' classification is appropriate rather than a deviation.

The inserted paragraph tracks the playbook model language and reaches the preferred position (up to 6 months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, deletion plus written certification), while correctly adapting the party name to 'IBM' and the defined term to 'Content' so it integrates with the agreement.
Placement is correct and minimal: appended to the termination paragraph without altering existing payment language, and the rationale notes § 14.2 survival already carries § 3.5 forward.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, explains the gap and the risk, and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing.
Deterministic checks pass and the changed text is additive only, consistent with an insert-type remedy.
